```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(r2parquet)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

We showcase how to upload tabular and spatial data to R2.

## Tabular data

As an example consider the geographic attributes file for the 2021 census. StatCan has disabled programmatic download, so the file has to be [downloaded manually](https://www12.statcan.gc.ca/census-recensement/alternative_alternatif.cfm?l=eng&dispext=zip&teng=2021_92-151_X.zip&k=%20%20%20%20%209602&loc=/census-recensement/2021/geo/aip-pia/attribute-attribs/files-fichiers/2021_92-151_X.zip) and the `download_path` parameter point to where the downloaded file lives.

```{r}
path <- file.path(params$download_path, "2021_92-151_X.csv")
```

The file has close to half a million rows, one per dissemination block, and takes 300 MB as CSV. Rather than reading it into R, we let DuckDB read it lazily, `data_to_parquet()` then writes lazy DuckDB tables with a single DuckDB `COPY` straight from the CSV to parquet, and uploads the parquet file in chunks, without the data ever passing through R.

Trial and error determined that the CSV is Windows-1252 encoded, which DuckDB reads via its `encodings` extension. We read all columns as text, otherwise DuckDB would turn codes like `SACCODE` `"001"` into numbers, and convert the numeric columns explicitly instead. The column names are bilingual, like `DBUID_IDIDU`, we keep the English part.

```{r}
csv_con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb())
DBI::dbExecute(csv_con, "INSTALL encodings") |> invisible()

geo_attributes <- tbl(csv_con, sql(paste0(
  "FROM read_csv(", DBI::dbQuoteString(csv_con, path), 
  ", encoding = 'cp1252', all_varchar = true)"))) |>
  rename_with(\(name) sub("_.*", "", name)) |>
  mutate(across(c(DBPOP2021, DBTDWELL2021, DBURDWELL2021), as.integer),
         across(c(DARPLAMX, DARPLAMY, DARPLAT, DARPLONG, DBAREA2021), as.numeric))

geo_attributes
```

Sorting by the dissemination block id keeps the blocks of each province, census division and subdivision together in the same row groups, so queries filtering on these only download the row groups they need.

```{r}
data_to_parquet(geo_attributes, "r2://test/census/2021/2021_92-151_X.parquet", 
                sort_by = "DBUID")

DBI::dbDisconnect(csv_con, shutdown = TRUE)
```

Reading it back, e.g. the population and dwellings by census subdivision in the Montréal CMA:

```{r}
parquet_tbl("r2://test/census/2021/2021_92-151_X.parquet") |>
  filter(CMAUID == "462") |>
  summarise(Population = sum(DBPOP2021, na.rm = TRUE), 
            Dwellings = sum(DBTDWELL2021, na.rm = TRUE),
            .by = CSDNAME) |>
  arrange(desc(Population)) |>
  collect()
```

## Spatial data

For this we consider hosting the StatCan metro area (CMA) level geographies from the 2021 census. StatCan has disabled programmatic download, so the geodatabase has to be [downloaded manually](https://www12.statcan.gc.ca/census-recensement/alternative_alternatif.cfm?l=eng&dispext=zip&teng=lcma000b21f_e.zip&k=%20%20%20%20%206393&loc=//www12.statcan.gc.ca/census-recensement/2021/geo/sip-pis/boundary-limites/files-fichiers/lcma000b21f_e.zip) and the `download_path` parameter set to the (unzipped) folder with the geodatabase.

We then read the data and cast it to MULTIPOLYGON. Some StatCan geography files contain MULTISURFACE geometries, which have to be converted before writing parquet files, for this file the cast does not change anything.

```{r, warning = FALSE}
d <- sf::st_read(file.path(params$download_path, "lcma000b21f_e/lcma000b21f_e.gdb"), quiet = TRUE) |>
  sf::st_cast("MULTIPOLYGON")
```

We then write this to a parquet file on R2, with the first path component being the bucket, which has to exist already (see `create_r2_bucket()` and the [Setting up R2](setting_up_r2.html) article for the credentials needed). Under the hood `data_to_parquet()` renames the geometry column to `geometry`, repairs invalid geometries, orders the rows by the `sort_by` columns, if any, and further along a Hilbert curve, and uploads the resulting GeoParquet file.

```{r}
data_to_parquet(d, "r2://test/census/2021/lcma000b21f_e.parquet", sort_by = "CMAUID")
```

The uploaded file can be queried lazily right away, here we read the Montréal CMA.

```{r montreal}
con <- parquet_tbl("r2://test/census/2021/lcma000b21f_e.parquet")

data <- con |>
  filter(CMAUID == "462") |>
  collect_sf()

ggplot(data) +
  geom_sf()
```
